title: He sounded like God…
paragraphs:
He sounded like God…
but died without Him.

Because this is not just his story.
This could be yours.

He was brilliant.
Respected.
Unmatched in insight.
When Ahithophel spoke, kings leaned in.
“The counsel that Ahithophel gave was as if one consulted the word of God.” — 2 Samuel 16:23

Not good advice.
Not wise suggestions.
The voice of God—that’s how people received him.

He ended his life alone, undone, hanging in silence.
— 2 Samuel 17:23
Here’s the tension you don’t want to face:

You can be spiritually impressive…
and still be spiritually dead.

You can know Scripture…
and not know the Savior.

You can guide others…
while your own soul is drifting into darkness.
When Absalom rebelled against King David, Ahithophel—David’s trusted advisor—betrayed him.
The Bible doesn’t spell out every motive.

But many scholars connect Ahithophel to Bathsheba’s family line (2 Samuel 11; 23:34).
Some scholars interpret that his betrayal may have been fueled by unresolved bitterness from David’s sin.
A silent fire burning beneath polished wisdom.
And here’s where it gets dangerously relatable.

You can carry pain so long…
that it starts to justify your pride.

You can nurture offense so deeply…
that it begins to rewrite your loyalty.
And when his counsel was rejected?
“When Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his donkey… set his house in order, and hanged himself.” — 2 Samuel 17:23
This is the danger of pride.

“I know what’s right.”
“I see clearly.”
“I don’t need correction.”
Pride doesn’t always look like rebellion.
Sometimes it looks like being right… without being surrendered.
And this is where the Gospel breaks in.
Because Ahithophel’s story doesn’t end with hope…
Not one who sounds like God…
“Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.” — 1 Corinthians 1:24
Ahithophel gave advice that shaped kingdoms.
Jesus gives words that raise the dead inside you.
Your greatest problem is not ignorance.
The moments you chose yourself over God.
And the solution is not becoming wiser.
Because no amount of insight can save you.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23

That includes the wise.
The respected.
The admired.
But here is the explosion of grace:
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
But while you were still broken…
And unlike Ahithophel—who ended in despair—
Jesus entered death and conquered it.
So no one has to end where pride leads.
Where is pride hiding in your life?

In your opinions?
Your wounds?
Your silent judgments?
Your need to be right?
Don’t wait until rejection exposes what humility could have healed.
Don’t let hidden pride write your ending.
Lay down your need to control.
Lay down your need to be right.
Lay down the version of yourself you’ve been protecting.

The kind that humbles you…
and heals you.
“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” — James 4:6
